prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D room layout and continuous approach across the five frames, starting with a downward view of the floor where the camera wearer's left hand (bottom, ~0.3 m) and a crouching person on the right (~0.7–1.0 m) reach toward an object on the floor within arm's reach of both. As the camera wearer looks up in frame 2 and walks forward through frames 3 to 5, the bright silhouette of a man seated in a chair shifts from mid-range (~2.0 m in frame 2, with the crouching person's shoulder still very bright at ~0.8 m in the bottom-right corner) to ~1.3 m in frame 3, and finally into immediate arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m, nearly white) as the camera wearer stands directly behind and above his back in frames 4 and 5. Behind and to the left/right of the seated man, the small wooden table and chairs sit ~0.3–0.5 m further back (~2.5–3.0 m from the camera in frame 2, closing to ~0.7–1.0 m on the right by frame 5) against a recessed left corner that appears very dark (~3.5+ m) while the wall and door on the right are nearer (~1.0–2.0 m). Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradients clearly separate the seated man's foreground silhouette from the similarly toned wall and tabletop behind him and clarify the stepped depth between the right-hand wall alcove and the deeper left background. However, the map is unreliable in frame 1 where the floor gradient flattens the crouching person's arm into the carpet, and in frames 4 and 5 where the right wall and the seated man's shoulders saturate to nearly identical bright values despite being at different distances.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities as the camera wearer moves from the floor interaction toward the seated man and his desk, though it misses the background walls, floor, and door entirely. In frame 1, a single pink `person` mask covers both the crouching person on the right (~0.7–1.0 m) and the object and camera wearer's hand at the bottom (~0.3–0.5 m), whereas frame 2 cleanly separates the seated `person` in the centre (~2.0 m, facing left) from the `chair` he sits on, the `dining table` (~2.5 m) behind his knees, and a second `chair` to the left (~2.8 m), while completely missing the partially visible crouching person at the bottom-right edge. In frame 3, as the camera wearer closes to ~1.3 m and the seated man looks toward the camera with his lower body cropped below the frame, masks appear for the `laptop` and `bottle` on the table (~1.6–1.8 m, within the seated man's arm's reach just behind his right shoulder) alongside the two `chair` masks, though the table itself is unlabelled. By frames 4 and 5, the seated `person` mask fills the lower-left and centre foreground (~0.4–0.7 m, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) facing away toward the table on the right, occluding the chair and left side of the table while leaving the `laptop` and tabletop items visible to his right (~0.6–0.9 m). While the masks help delineate overlapping furniture and small tabletop items (such as the spray `bottle` in frame 3) against cluttered RGB backgrounds, the map is unreliable where it merges multiple bodies and bags in frame 1, drops the table mask after frame 2, and misclassifies the bright tablet screen on the right edge of the table as a `remote` in frame 4 and a `mouse` in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks skeletal keypoints only for the seated man in frames 2, 3, and 4, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons in frames 1 and 5 despite people and hands being within ~0.3–1.0 m of the camera wearer. In frame 2, a yellow torso-and-leg skeleton in left profile (with a cluster of head keypoints at the top and a dense magenta hand cluster resting on his knees) shows the man seated ~2.0 m ahead in the centre of the room, facing left with his head angled slightly toward the camera wearer and his hands within reach of his lap and the adjacent table. In frame 3, as the camera wearer approaches to ~1.3 m and the man's lower body passes out of view below the bottom edge, only a tight cluster of yellow facial/head keypoints (~1.3 m) and two neck/shoulder points remain, indicating that his head is turned toward the camera wearer while his torso and arms are unmapped. In frame 4, when the camera wearer is ~0.6 m behind and above him, the map shows left-profile facial keypoints facing left away from the camera and a single yellow shoulder-to-shoulder bar across his upper back, capturing his 90-degree head-and-torso turn away from the camera wearer toward the table on the right. Although the pose keypoints in frame 2 clarify the exact joint articulation of the seated man's folded hands and bent knees against his dark trousers in the blurry RGB image, the map is highly unreliable across the sequence due to complete missed detections under severe egocentric viewing angles and partial body cropping in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5.
